How the screen is composed

The visible terminal is assembled from the components in crates/cli/src/tui/components/. Those components draw a distinction between durable conversation, live activity, focused detail, and a decision that needs your input.

Live work becomes a record

ComponentWhat you seeWhy it exists
message.rsUser prompts and assistant output.Keeps the conversation spine readable.
activity_rail.rsLive thinking/work rail for a turn.Shows progress without permanently expanding the transcript.
tool_row.rs□ running, ✓ complete, × failed.Makes each local action visible and inspectable.
subagent_row.rsIndented worker activity, provider/model identity, and nested tools.Shows delegated work as part of the parent action.
progress_list.rsThe task list and current progress.Shows the plan the agent is following.

While work is live, failures expand inline. Once a turn completes, the activity rail collapses into a compact summary; press ctrl+o to expand the full tree, or use /expand <n> for a recent tool result.

Focus and decisions

ComponentUser-facing behavior
inspector.rsIn split view, shows the selected tool’s concise summary or exact debug input/output.
picker.rs + tray.rsReusable keyboard-driven pickers for providers, models, sessions, themes, MCP, skills, extensions, and subagent settings.
ask.rsStructured clarification form when the agent needs a choice before continuing.
notification.rsShort status notices without rewriting the transcript.
composer.rs + status_bar.rsThe input surface and persistent operating state: mode, context, background work, and workspace.

Approvals take priority over ordinary overlays. That is intentional: when a tool wants to act, the decision cannot be hidden behind a picker or notification.

Controls that expose the components

ctrl+o        expand or collapse a turn’s activity tree
/expand 1     show full output for the latest tool call
/settings     open configuration pickers
/subagents    open the worker configuration tray
/mcp          open the MCP server picker
/skills       open the skills picker
/todo         show the task progress list

The UI components are deliberately narrow renderers. The application state and event handlers decide what is active; components turn that state into terminal lines. This keeps a picker, a tool row, or a subagent record consistent everywhere it appears.
